metric_parameters.explanation: Methods longer than this many lines may be too complex and should be refactored.

metric_notes.definition: Flags functions whose meaningful (non-comment) lines exceed LONG_METHOD_LINES, indicating excessive length and likely excessive responsibility.

calculation.raw_calculation: Reload each module_record's path to read raw lines, then for every module_level_functions entry count the non-blank, non-# lines between lineno and tolineno (falling back to lineno when tolineno is null) and flag whenever that trimmed count exceeds LONG_METHOD_LINES (45).
calculation.inputs: code.files[].module_level_functions[].name, .lineno, and .tolineno, plus code.files[].path so the source text can be re-read, and the LONG_METHOD_LINES parameter.
calculation.limitations: Only module_level_functions are reported by the extractor, so class methods, nested defs, and dynamically added callables do not participate. The extractor also omits decorator metadata, so the re-parsed source must assume every reported function is a candidate (property getters and setters cannot be filtered without additional payload). Comment filtering is limited to stripped lines that begin with "#", so multiline strings and docstrings still contribute to the row count, and the only available start/end markers are lineno/tolineno, so syntax errors or missing tolineno values force a conservative fallback.

result_guide.Name: Long Method
result_guide.Description: Method '<name>' has <non_comment_loc> non-comment lines (> LONG_METHOD_LINES).

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with more than this many methods may have too many responsibilities.

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes that define more than LARGE_CLASS_METHODS non-trivial methods, suggesting the class holds too many responsibilities.

calculation.raw_calculation: Iterate every class reported inside code.files; skip bases ending with 'Exception', count the non-dunder names in class_methods, and flag whenever that count exceeds LARGE_CLASS_METHODS (15).
calculation.inputs: code.files[].classes[].name, .bases, .class_methods, .lineno, and .path plus the LARGE_CLASS_METHODS threshold.
calculation.limitations: Class entries lack decorator metadata and method bodies, so dataclasses cannot be excluded and every listed method is counted even if it is a simple getter/setter; this leads to an overestimate of non-trivial methods compared to the detector that inspects method bodies.

result_guide.Name: Large Class
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' has <non_trivial_methods> non-trivial methods (> LARGE_CLASS_METHODS).

metric_parameters.explanation: Functions with more than this many primitive parameters may benefit from introducing parameter objects.
Minimum number of arguments required before primitive-obsession detection runs.
Minimum fraction of primitive-typed parameters to flag primitive obsession.

metric_notes.definition: Flags functions that overuse primitive-typed parameters, exceeding both count and ratio thresholds, indicating a missing richer data structure.

calculation.raw_calculation: For each module_level_functions entry, skip anything with total parameter count at or below PRIMITIVE_MIN_ARGS, then count arguments whose annotations decode to primitive types (int, str, float, bool), compute the primitive_ratio after discounting a leading 'self' when present, and raise a medium flag whenever that primitive count exceeds PRIMITIVE_OBSESSION_COUNT and the primitive_ratio exceeds PRIMITIVE_RATIO_THRESHOLD.
calculation.inputs: code.files[].module_level_functions[].name, .param_names, .lineno, and file paths plus the expected annotation list that mirrors astroid's node.args.annotations, together with parameters PRIMITIVE_MIN_ARGS, PRIMITIVE_OBSESSION_COUNT, and PRIMITIVE_RATIO_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: The extractor currently only emits param_names for module_level_functions, so there is no field equivalent to node.args.annotations or any method-level entries (classes/methods are omitted), meaning we cannot actually identify which parameters are primitive typed; this approximation depends on extending the facts payload with annotation metadata and on the fact that only top-level functions show up in this stream.

result_guide.Name: Primitive Obsession
result_guide.Description: Uses <primitive_group_size> primitives together (min args PRIMITIVE_MIN_ARGS, ratio <primitive_ratio> > PRIMITIVE_RATIO_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Functions with more than this many parameters may be trying to do too much.

metric_notes.definition: Flags functions whose parameter count (after dropping self) exceeds LONG_PARAMETER_LIST, signaling the function interface is too wide.

calculation.raw_calculation: Browse every module_level_functions entry, drop a leading 'self' if present to mirror method counting, compare the remaining parameter count against LONG_PARAMETER_LIST, and raise a medium flag whenever that head-count exceeds the configured threshold (5).
calculation.inputs: code.files[].module_level_functions[].name, .param_names, .lineno, and .path together with the LONG_PARAMETER_LIST threshold.
calculation.limitations: Only module_level_functions entries exist in the current facts payload, so class methods and nested functions never surface and constructors are only detected by name; there are also no fields for node.args.vararg/node.args.kwarg, meaning the detector's +2 threshold allowance for functions that accept *args/**kwargs cannot be reproduced here.

result_guide.Name: Long Parameter List
result_guide.Description: Function '<name>' has <param_count> parameters (> LONG_PARAMETER_LIST).

metric_parameters.explanation: Groups of parameters appearing together in multiple functions may indicate data clumps.
Minimum parameter-group size to consider for data clumps.

metric_notes.definition: Flags repeated groups of parameters appearing together across multiple functions, indicating tightly coupled data that should be encapsulated.

calculation.raw_calculation: Within each file_entry, skip constructors, drop a leading 'self', and for each subset of parameters sized between DATA_CLUMP_MIN_COMBO_SIZE and the function's arity accumulate which functions share that subset; once a subset is reused in more than one function and itself contains at least DATA_CLUMPS_THRESHOLD names, raise a medium flag for that group and attach the functions and module path to the finding.
calculation.inputs: code.files[].module_level_functions[].name, .param_names, and .path combined with thresholds DATA_CLUMPS_THRESHOLD and DATA_CLUMP_MIN_COMBO_SIZE, using itertools-style parameter combinations.
calculation.limitations: Only module_level_functions are available in the AST output, so class methods, including properties and constructors (beyond name matching '__init__'), never contribute, and there is no decorator metadata to filter actual properties; the extractor also lacks annotations or usage info, so detection relies purely on repeating parameter names and cannot confirm deeper semantic similarity.

result_guide.Name: Data Clumps
result_guide.Description: Group <group_members> recurs <occurrences> times (>= DATA_CLUMPS_THRESHOLD, size >= DATA_CLUMP_MIN_COMBO_SIZE).

metric_parameters.explanation: If-else chains longer than this may indicate a switch statement smell.

metric_notes.definition: Flags switch-like constructs (nested if/elif chains) that indicate missing polymorphism or dispatch abstraction.

calculation.raw_calculation: Traverse every AST module for `If` nodes with an `orelse` section, skip those nested in exception handlers, count chained branches by walking `orelse` entries that are themselves `If` nodes, then bypass guard clauses and simple `isinstance` type switches before flagging any branch count that exceeds COMPLEX_CONDITIONAL as a medium severity issue.
calculation.inputs: AST-level `nodes.If` instances with their `orelse`, `body`, `test`, and `lineno` metadata, plus the configured COMPLEX_CONDITIONAL threshold and the corresponding module file path; these nodes are not part of the current code_payload, which only exposes module_level_functions[] and classes[].
calculation.limitations: None of the extracted facts expose AST `If` nodes or any information about conditional chains, so this metric cannot actually run without extending the extractor to capture branching structures and exception ancestry.

result_guide.Name: Switch Statements
result_guide.Description: Conditional chain has <branch_count> branches (> COMPLEX_CONDITIONAL) or repeated switch logic.

metric_parameters.explanation: Fields initialized but not used in most methods may be temporary fields.

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes that initialize fields which are never or rarely used across methods, indicating transient state that should be localized or removed.

calculation.raw_calculation: For each class entry, skip exception subclasses, subtract attributes marked as used or cached (plus the standard ignored names) from the collected init_fields, and flag the remaining names whenever their count meets or exceeds TEMPORARY_FIELD_THRESHOLD.
calculation.inputs: code.files[].classes[].name, .bases, .lineno, and file path together with measured sets named init_fields, used_fields, cached_fields, and the TEMPORARY_FIELD_THRESHOLD parameter.
calculation.limitations: The extractor currently only reports class names, base names, and method lists, so there is no data for init_fields/used_fields/cached_fields or decorator metadata; without the per-attribute assignments and usage counts the metric cannot actually run and would need a richer AST payload to identify temporary fields.

result_guide.Name: Temporary Field
result_guide.Description: Field '<field>' is used by <consumer_count> methods (< TEMPORARY_FIELD_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with identical sets of methods may be alternative classes with different interfaces.

metric_notes.definition: Flags multiple classes that offer similar behaviors via overlapping method sets but with no shared abstraction, suggesting duplicated concepts behind differing interfaces.

calculation.raw_calculation: Group classes by their filtered public method names (ignoring private and dunder helpers), drop groups with fewer than ALTERNATIVE_CLASSES_THRESHOLD members, and raise a medium findership whenever a group has no overlapping base names so the similarity cannot be explained by inheritance.
calculation.inputs: code.files[].classes[].name, .bases, .class_methods, .lineno, and .path together with ALTERNATIVE_CLASSES_THRESHOLD; method sets are derived from the class_methods list.
calculation.limitations: The payload only exposes class names, base lists, and method names, so we cannot inspect decorators for dataclass/abstract exclusions, cannot distinguish property declarations or inherited helpers, and cannot reproduce the detector's mymethods() logic that evaluates actual AST nodes.

result_guide.Name: Alternative Classes with Different Interfaces
result_guide.Description: Classes <class_a>/<class_b> share capability but have > ALTERNATIVE_CLASSES_THRESHOLD interface mismatches.

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with more than this many distinct method name prefixes may be changing for too many reasons.
Classes with more than this many methods changing for different reasons may have divergent change.

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes that accumulate methods for many unrelated responsibilities (diverse prefixes), implying the class would need to change for multiple reasons.

calculation.pseudo-code:
from collections import defaultdict
for file_entry in code_payload['data']['files']:
    class_prefix_groups = defaultdict(lambda: {'prefixes': [], 'methods': []})
    for cls in file_entry['classes']:
        if any(base.endswith(('Exception', 'ABC')) for base in cls['bases']):
            continue
        method_prefixes = []
        for method_name in cls['class_methods']:
            if (method_name.startswith('__') or method_name.startswith('_') or
                method_name in {'__init__', '__str__', '__repr__', '__eq__', '__hash__'}):
                continue
            prefix = method_name.split('_')[0]
            if prefix in {'get', 'set', 'is', 'has', 'validate', 'create', 'update', 'delete'}:
                continue
            method_prefixes.append(prefix)
        class_prefix_groups[cls['name']]['prefixes'].extend(method_prefixes)
        class_prefix_groups[cls['name']]['methods'].extend([method_name for method_name in cls['class_methods'] if method_name not in {'__init__'}])
    for cls_name, data in class_prefix_groups.items():
        unique_prefixes = set(data['prefixes'])
        if (len(unique_prefixes) > DIVERGENT_CHANGE_PREFIXES and
            len(data['methods']) > DIVERGENT_CHANGE_METHODS):
            emit a medium-severity flag for cls_name at file_entry['path'] noting len(unique_prefixes) prefixes and len(data['methods']) method entries
calculation.raw_calculation: On each class entry, filter base names for exceptions and ABCs, then count every method name that survives the private/magic and common-prefix filters, compute the unique prefix set from the remaining method names, and flag the class whenever the unique prefix count exceeds DIVERGENT_CHANGE_PREFIXES and the filtered method count exceeds DIVERGENT_CHANGE_METHODS.
calculation.inputs: code.files[].classes[].name, .bases, .class_methods, .lineno, and .path together with DIVERGENT_CHANGE_PREFIXES and DIVERGENT_CHANGE_METHODS; method names come from the class_methods list in the AST payload.
calculation.limitations: The extractor only provides method name lists and class base names, so decorator-driven decisions (dataclass, property) and mixin detection are impossible, and there is no way to know which methods were inherited versus defined locally, making this an approximation of the detector's AST-based logic.

result_guide.Name: Potential Divergent Change
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' has <group_count> change groups; largest group size <largest_group> (> DIVERGENT_CHANGE_METHODS).

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum similarity between method sets to consider hierarchies parallel.

metric_notes.definition: Flags inheritance trees that mirror each other with similarly named subclasses and overlapping method sets, indicating duplicated evolution across parallel hierarchies.

calculation.raw_calculation: Group classes by their base names to build hierarchies, skip Exception/mixin families, check for any pair of hierarchies that each have at least two derived classes, share a naming suffix after the root, and whose representative method sets overlap above PARALLEL_INHERITANCE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD, and flag those combinations as high-severity parallel hierarchies at the module path.
calculation.inputs: code.files[].classes[].name, .bases, .class_methods, and .path plus the PARALLEL_INHERITANCE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD parameter, treating class_methods as the method name list for each class.
calculation.limitations: The code facts payload only lists class names, base names, and method names (no decorators or AST nodes), so the detector's dataclass/abstract exclusions, mixin naming checks, and actual AST `.mymethods()` calculations cannot be reproduced; method similarity therefore relies solely on the provided name sets.

result_guide.Name: Parallel Inheritance Hierarchies
result_guide.Description: Hierarchies <hier_a>/<hier_b> similarity <similarity> (> PARALLEL_INHERITANCE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum number of calls to consider potential shotgun surgery.
Minimum number of contexts where calls appear to consider potential shotgun surgery.
Common utility names to exclude.

metric_notes.definition: Flags functions whose calls are scattered across many contexts, hinting that a change would require edits in numerous places (shotgun surgery risk).

calculation.raw_calculation: Iterate every AST module, gather each `nodes.Call` whose callee is a named symbol that is not in SHOTGUN_SURGERY_EXCLUDE_NAMES, remember the line numbers plus the first enclosing function/class name, and raise a high flag whenever a method is called at least SHOTGUN_SURGERY_CALLS times across at least SHOTGUN_SURGERY_CONTEXTS distinct contexts.
calculation.inputs: `nodes.Call` entries with `func.name`, `lineno`, and the enclosing `nodes.FunctionDef`/`nodes.ClassDef` names per module, as well as module file paths, plus the SHOTGUN_SURGERY_CALLS, SHOTGUN_SURGERY_CONTEXTS, and SHOTGUN_SURGERY_EXCLUDE_NAMES parameters.
calculation.limitations: The current extractor only emits module-level summaries (module_level_functions and class declarations) and no AST call records or ancestor metadata, so the described detection cannot execute until the call/ancestor information is added to the facts payload.

result_guide.Name: Potential Shotgun Surgery
result_guide.Description: Change touches <call_count> calls or <context_count> contexts (> SHOTGUN_SURGERY_CALLS/SHOTGUN_SURGERY_CONTEXTS).

metric_parameters.explanation: Comment-to-code ratio threshold.
Minimum large comment blocks.

metric_notes.definition: Flags files where comment density is unusually high or dominated by large comment blocks, suggesting code that may be unclear or outdated.

calculation.raw_calculation: Re-read each file_path from the payload, identify contiguous comment sequences, count meaningful code lines (skipping blank lines and docstrings), compute the ratio of comment lines to code lines, count comment blocks longer than LARGE_COMMENT_BLOCKS, and raise the flag whenever the ratio exceeds EXCESSIVE_COMMENTS_RATIO and the large-block count exceeds its threshold.
calculation.inputs: code.files[].path so the raw file text can be re-read, plus EXCESSIVE_COMMENTS_RATIO and LARGE_COMMENT_BLOCKS.
calculation.limitations: The extractor only reports AST structure (module-level classes/functions) and no line-by-line content, so the described comment counts require re-reading the source file and cannot be supplied directly by the existing facts payload.

result_guide.Name: Excessive Comments
result_guide.Description: Comment density <comment_ratio> (> EXCESSIVE_COMMENTS_RATIO) or block length <block_len> (> LARGE_COMMENT_BLOCKS).

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum number of similar code blocks to consider duplication.
Minimum lines in a code block to consider for duplication.

metric_notes.definition: Flags repeated code blocks appearing in multiple places, indicating copy-paste duplication that should be consolidated.

calculation.raw_calculation: Normalize each FunctionDef by replacing identifiers with placeholders and stripping whitespace/comments, group functions with identical normalized bodies, skip functions shorter than DUPLICATE_CODE_MIN_LINES, tests, and simple getters/setters, then flag whenever a normalized block appears in at least DUPLICATE_CODE_THRESHOLD functions using the shared file path and total line counts for context.
calculation.inputs: AST `nodes.FunctionDef` entries with their `name`, `body` (for length, statement kind, ancestor comments), and containing module file path plus thresholds DUPLICATE_CODE_MIN_LINES and DUPLICATE_CODE_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: Only module_level_functions metadata exists in the current extractor output (no AST FunctionDef nodes, bodies, or normalized source), so the actual duplicate detection cannot run until those AST nodes and body contents are serialized.

result_guide.Name: Duplicate Code
result_guide.Description: Duplicate block length <lines> similarity <similarity> (>= DUPLICATE_CODE_THRESHOLD) across locations <locations>.

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum getters/setters to consider a data class.

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes that primarily store data and expose only trivial getters/setters, lacking meaningful behavior.

calculation.raw_calculation: Iterate every ClassDef, skip dataclasses and Exception subclasses, tally getters/setters by name prefix and single-statement bodies while ignoring magic methods, and when a class has no non-trivial methods, at least DATA_CLASS_METHODS true getters/setters, and no common data-class suffix, emit a medium finding referencing the class name and file path.
calculation.inputs: `nodes.ClassDef` entries with their decorators, base names, `name`, `lineno`, and the `mymethods()` list (each method providing `name` and `body` length) together with the DATA_CLASS_METHODS threshold.
calculation.limitations: The current AST facts only list high-level class_name/bases/method_names without decorator information, bodies, or MethodDef node details, so this detection cannot run on those payloads and requires richer AST exports before emitting results.

result_guide.Name: Data Class
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' has <non_trivial_methods> non-trivial methods (<= DATA_CLASS_METHODS) and mostly holds data.

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum unused functions to flag dead code.

metric_notes.definition: Flags code elements (functions or utilities) that are defined but never used, indicating removable dead code.

calculation.raw_calculation: Scan every AST module to register each FunctionDef except tests/properties, record whether decorators suggest external exposure, track all callees (both Name and Attribute), and when a function is neither called nor marked public/exported and at least DEAD_CODE_THRESHOLD such functions exist, report all of them as dead code for that file.
calculation.inputs: AST `nodes.FunctionDef` metadata (name, decorators, body for detecting calls and property flags), all contained `nodes.Call` entries with `func.name` or `func.attrname`, plus module_record.file_path and the DEAD_CODE_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: The supplied AST facts only describe module_level_functions and simple class summaries; there are no FunctionDef bodies, decorator data, or call-site lists, so this metric cannot be computed without enriching the extractor payload with those detailed nodes.

result_guide.Name: Dead Code
result_guide.Description: Symbol '<name>' is unused (unused count > DEAD_CODE_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Maximum non-trivial methods to consider a class lazy.
Maximum total lines of non-trivial methods to consider a class lazy.

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes with minimal behavior (few non-trivial methods or lines), suggesting the class adds little value and should be collapsed or removed.

calculation.raw_calculation: Every ClassDef is inspected (skipping known small suffixes and dataclasses), its public/non-trivial methods are filtered via values returned by `mymethods()`, and whenever the surviving method count is at or below LAZY_CLASS_METHODS and their cumulative line span is at or below LAZY_CLASS_LINES, the class is reported as lazy with the path, class name, method count, and total line span.
calculation.inputs: Astroid `nodes.ClassDef` records including `name`, `bases`, `decorators`, `lineno`, and each `mymethods()` entry’s `name`, `body`, `fromlineno`, and `tolineno`, plus module file paths and the LAZY_CLASS_METHODS/LAZY_CLASS_LINES thresholds.
calculation.limitations: The current extractor only returns class names/bases/method name lists (no decorator data, no `mymethods()` bodies, and no fromlineno/tolineno ranges), so this detection cannot yet run on the available payload and would need richer AST exports to determine non-trivial method counts and total line spans.

result_guide.Name: Lazy Class
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' has <methods> methods and <loc> LOC below LAZY_CLASS thresholds.

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum empty methods to consider speculative generality.
Minimum unused parameters to consider speculative generality.

metric_notes.definition: Flags abstractions added for possible future use—empty hooks, placeholder methods, or unused parameters—that bloat the design without current value.

calculation.raw_calculation: Each ClassDef is analyzed (skipping known ABC/interface patterns), empty/pass methods are counted, and every method collects the names of its parameter list minus 'self' and intersected with names referenced inside the method body to find unused parameters; a medium finding is raised whenever the number of empty methods or unused parameters crosses SPECULATIVE_GENERALITY_THRESHOLD or UNUSED_PARAMETERS_THRESHOLD respectively.
calculation.inputs: AST `nodes.ClassDef` entries with their base names, decorators, `name`, and contained methods (via `mymethods()` providing `name`, `body`, `args`, and `nodes_of_class(nodes.Name)`), plus module file paths and thresholds SPECULATIVE_GENERALITY_THRESHOLD / UNUSED_PARAMETERS_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: The currently available AST facts only list name lists for classes/methods; there is no decorator, `mymethods()`, method body, or parameter usage information, so this detector cannot actually compute unused parameters or empty methods without richer payloads.

result_guide.Name: Speculative Generality
result_guide.Description: Unused hooks/parameters count <speculative_count> exceeds SPECULATIVE_GENERALITY/UNUSED_PARAMETERS thresholds.

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum calls to an external class to consider feature envy.
Ratio of external to local calls to consider feature envy.

metric_notes.definition: Flags methods that rely more on another object’s data than their own, signaling misplaced behavior that should move closer to the envied class.

calculation.raw_calculation: Visit every AST FunctionDef, skip properties and trivial getters, count Attribute accesses by their owning expression, track how many self-calls vs external-object calls each method makes, and whenever the most-called external target exceeds FEATURE_ENVY_CALLS and the same count outpaces local accesses by FEATURE_ENVY_LOCAL_RATIO, flag the method.
calculation.inputs: AST `nodes.FunctionDef` nodes with decorators and their `nodes.Attribute` references (each with `expr.name` and `attrname`), `func.lineno`, module file paths, and thresholds FEATURE_ENVY_CALLS / FEATURE_ENVY_LOCAL_RATIO.
calculation.limitations: The extractor only emits module_level_functions and classes without decorators, Attribute usages, or return/body information, so feature-envy detection needs those AST nodes and cannot run on the current payload.

result_guide.Name: Feature Envy
result_guide.Description: Method '<name>' foreign/local access ratio <ratio> (> FEATURE_ENVY_LOCAL_RATIO) with <foreign_calls> foreign calls (> FEATURE_ENVY_CALLS).

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum shared members to consider inappropriate intimacy.
Method ratio threshold for inappropriate intimacy.

metric_notes.definition: Flags pairs of classes that are overly coupled by sharing many members or calling each other’s internals, indicating excessive exposure between modules.

calculation.raw_calculation: Collect every ClassDef’s non-magic methods and exposed instance attributes, track inheritance/composition links through base names and assigned attributes, and for each unrelated class pair compute how many of class A’s methods touch class B’s fields; if the shared-member count and shared/total-method ratio surpass the configured thresholds, flag class A’s intimacy with class B using the module path.
calculation.inputs: `nodes.ClassDef` entries with their `name`, decorator lists, `mymethods()` results (method names), `instance_attrs`, base classes, and assigned attribute expressions, plus the INAPPROPRIATE_INTIMACY_SHARED and INAPPROPRIATE_INTIMACY_METHOD_RATIO thresholds and module file paths.
calculation.limitations: The extractor currently only reports class names, base lists, and method name arrays, so there are no instance attribute sets, decorator data, or composition relationships available—without those AST details this metric cannot be evaluated from the existing facts payload.

result_guide.Name: Inappropriate Intimacy
result_guide.Description: Classes <class_a>/<class_b> share <shared_members> internals or method ratio <ratio> exceeds intimacy thresholds.

metric_parameters.explanation: Maximum allowed chain length before flagging.

metric_notes.definition: Flags long call/attribute chains that navigate through multiple objects to reach data, signaling tight coupling and train-wreck accessors.

calculation.raw_calculation: For each AST Attribute chain detected, count how many Attribute hops connect to a root name, ignore chains shorter than MESSAGE_CHAIN_LENGTH or those classified as builder/common patterns, derive the first surrounding function/class for context, and flag the remaining chains with their length and the composed access path if they exceed the threshold.
calculation.inputs: `nodes.Attribute` entries with their `attrname`, `expr`, ancestor stack, and `lineno`, along with the MESSAGE_CHAIN_LENGTH threshold and module file paths; the builder/common-pattern helper predicates use conventional name lists.
calculation.limitations: The extractor only emits module_level_functions and classes with names/method lists and no attribute-chain data or ancestor information, so this calculation cannot be performed until Attribute chains and ancestor context are serialized.

result_guide.Name: Message Chains
result_guide.Description: Call/attribute chain length <chain_length> (> MESSAGE_CHAIN_LENGTH).

metric_parameters.explanation: Delegation ratio threshold for middle man.
Maximum delegate targets to consider middle man.

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes whose methods primarily delegate work to other objects, adding little behavior of their own.

calculation.raw_calculation: Skip classes that already identify as proxies/adapters (name suffixes or very small bodies), build the full method list via `mymethods()`, ignore properties/magic methods, count delegates that simply return a call, track each unique object they delegate to, and flag the class whenever the delegating-method ratio surpasses MIDDLE_MAN_RATIO while the number of delegate targets stays within MIDDLE_MAN_MAX_DELEGATE_TARGETS.
calculation.inputs: Astroid `nodes.ClassDef` metadata containing `name`, `body`, decorators, and the `mymethods()` entries; each method’s `body` statements, `decorators`, `name`, and any `nodes.Return`/`nodes.Call` chain so the delegate target string can be recorded, plus module file paths and the MIDDLE_MAN_RATIO and MIDDLE_MAN_MAX_DELEGATE_TARGETS thresholds.
calculation.limitations: The current AST extractor only supplies module_level_functions and class name/method lists without decorator data, method bodies, or return-call structure, so computing delegation ratios and identifying return-call delegates requires richer AST payloads that are not yet emitted.

result_guide.Name: Middle Man
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' delegates <delegation_ratio>% of methods to <= <delegate_targets> targets (> MIDDLE_MAN_RATIO).

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum modules to consider hub analysis.
Connection ratio threshold for hub-like dependencies.
Minimum connections to consider hub-like dependency.
Minimum fan-in/out balance ratio.
Maximum fan-in/out balance ratio.

metric_notes.definition: Flags modules that act as oversized hubs with many inbound/outbound (and external) dependencies and unbalanced traffic, creating central points of failure.

calculation.pseudo-code:
total_nodes = len(module_dependency_graph.nodes())
if total_nodes < HUB_MIN_PROJECT_MODULES:
    return
threshold = HUB_LIKE_DEPENDENCY_THRESHOLD
min_connections = MIN_HUB_CONNECTIONS
bal_min = HUB_BALANCE_RATIO_MIN
bal_max = HUB_BALANCE_RATIO_MAX
for module in module_dependency_graph.nodes():
    in_degree = module_dependency_graph.in_degree(module)
    out_degree = module_dependency_graph.out_degree(module)
    external_deps = len(module_external_dependencies.get(module, []))
    total_connections = in_degree + out_degree + external_deps
    if total_connections < min_connections:
        continue
    connection_ratio = total_connections / total_nodes
    if connection_ratio <= threshold:
        continue
    if any(pattern in module.lower() for pattern in ['util', 'common', 'base', 'core']):
        continue
    fan_in_ratio = in_degree / total_nodes if total_nodes else 0
    fan_out_ratio = (out_degree + external_deps) / total_nodes if total_nodes else 0
    balance_ratio = fan_in_ratio / fan_out_ratio if fan_out_ratio else (float('inf') if fan_in_ratio > 0 else 0)
    if not (bal_min <= balance_ratio <= bal_max):
        emit flag severity='high' if total_connections > min_connections * 2 else 'medium' referencing module and computed fan ratios
calculation.raw_calculation: From the module dependency graph plus recorded external dependencies, ignore analysis when the project is too small, then for each module count internal in/out degrees and external points, filter out lightweight utilities, check that its total connections exceed MIN_HUB_CONNECTIONS and that the fraction of connections per total nodes exceeds HUB_LIKE_DEPENDENCY_THRESHOLD, compute the loose fan-in/fan-out ratio, and when the ratio escapes the [HUB_BALANCE_RATIO_MIN, HUB_BALANCE_RATIO_MAX] window report the module as a hub (escalating to high severity for modules with more than twice the minimum connections).
calculation.inputs: module_dependency_graph.nodes()/edges to expose in_degree/out_degree, module_external_dependencies[module] lists for external deps, module file paths, and thresholds: HUB_MIN_PROJECT_MODULES, HUB_LIKE_DEPENDENCY_THRESHOLD, MIN_HUB_CONNECTIONS, HUB_BALANCE_RATIO_MIN, HUB_BALANCE_RATIO_MAX.
calculation.limitations: The available AST/structural facts do not currently include a full module dependency graph or the external dependency counts per module, so the hub-like calculation described here requires adding dependency graph outputs (with in/out degrees) and recorded external dependencies to the extractor payload.

result_guide.Name: Hub-like Dependency
result_guide.Description: Module '<module>' degree <degree> (> HUB_LIKE_DEPENDENCY_THRESHOLD) across <module_count> modules, balance within HUB_BALANCE ratios.

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum function name length to consider.
Function names to exclude.
Minimum occurrences across modules to consider scattered.

metric_notes.definition: Flags features whose implementation is scattered across many modules (same function appearing in multiple places), indicating cross-cutting code and weak cohesion.

calculation.raw_calculation: Group each module’s public function names (filtered by length, excluded labels, and private prefixes) using the module_functions map; whenever the same function name appears in at least MIN_SCATTERED_OCCURRENCES distinct modules, flag that function as scattered by reporting the modules it spans and the module path for the first occurrence.
calculation.inputs: module_functions mapping (module -> list of function names), module_paths lookup for reporting, and thresholds SCATTERED_MIN_FUNCTION_NAME_LENGTH, SCATTERED_EXCLUDED_NAMES, and MIN_SCATTERED_OCCURRENCES.
calculation.limitations: The code facts extractor only captures module_level_functions without the architectural module_functions map or module dependency records, so this detection requires those aggregated dictionaries and per-module file paths to be emitted by the architectural extractor.

result_guide.Name: Scattered Functionality
result_guide.Description: Feature '<feature>' spans <module_count> modules (>= MIN_SCATTERED_OCCURRENCES).

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum functions in a module to consider redundancy.
Function set similarity threshold to consider redundancy.

metric_notes.definition: Flags modules exposing largely overlapping public APIs, suggesting duplicated or redundant abstractions that could be merged.

calculation.raw_calculation: Aggregate each module’s filtered public function list, group modules that expose the same function set signature (after removing private/test helpers and requiring at least REDUNDANT_MIN_FUNCTIONS members), then for every pair among the matching modules compute the Jaccard similarity of their function sets and flag the pair whenever the score meets or exceeds REDUNDANT_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD, referencing the first module’s file path in the finding.
calculation.inputs: module_functions mapping (module -> set of function names) and module_paths map for file reporting plus thresholds REDUNDANT_MIN_FUNCTIONS and REDUNDANT_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: The existing code facts only list per-file module_level_functions without the aggregated module_functions map or module_paths lookup, so this architectural detection requires those aggregated structures (and the ability to compute per-module function sets) before it can be executed.

result_guide.Name: Potential Redundant Abstractions
result_guide.Description: Modules <module_a>/<module_b> share <shared_functions> functions with similarity <similarity> (>= REDUNDANT_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum public functions to consider god object.
Function count threshold for god object.

metric_notes.definition: Flags monolithic modules/classes with too many public responsibilities, behaving as god objects that centralize diverse functionality.

calculation.raw_calculation: For each module in module_functions, collect all public candidates (drop private names, short names, and known test/setup/common prefixes), check that the remaining set has at least MIN_GOD_OBJECT_FUNCTIONS entries and exceeds GOD_OBJECT_FUNCTIONS, and raise a medium severity smell describing the public function count and module path.
calculation.inputs: module_functions mapping (module -> set/list of function names), module_paths lookup for file path reporting, and thresholds MIN_GOD_OBJECT_FUNCTIONS plus GOD_OBJECT_FUNCTIONS.
calculation.limitations: The current architectural facts only emit aggregated module names and counts indirectly; there is no module_functions map or module_paths lookup in the existing payload, so this detection requires those structures to be serialized before the metric can truly execute.

result_guide.Name: God Object
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' has <fields> fields and <methods> behaviors (> GOD_OBJECT_FUNCTIONS and MIN_GOD_OBJECT_FUNCTIONS).

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum API calls to consider repetition.
Repetition ratio threshold.
Minimum count per call to consider repetitive.

metric_notes.definition: Flags modules that heavily call a single external API in a repetitive way, suggesting over-reliance or misplacement of that usage.

calculation.raw_calculation: Use the architectural module_api_usage map to examine each module’s recorded API calls, skip modules with fewer than MIN_API_CALLS overall, count how often each external API name appears, keep only calls repeated at least API_REPETITION_MIN_COUNT times, compute the ratio of those repeated calls to the total call volume, and when that ratio surpasses API_REPETITION_THRESHOLD flag the module with its repetition ratio and the repeating API names.
calculation.inputs: module_api_usage[module] lists of API call identifiers, module_paths[module] for the file path, plus MIN_API_CALLS, API_REPETITION_MIN_COUNT, and API_REPETITION_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: Current AST/structural facts only emit module_level_functions/class summaries without the architectural module_api_usage map or recorded API call series, so this detection cannot execute until the extractor returns per-module API call histories.

result_guide.Name: Potential Improper API Usage
result_guide.Description: Client call sequence deviates (calls <call_count> vs MIN_API_CALLS or repetition exceeds API_REPETITION thresholds).

metric_parameters.explanation: Module names to exclude from orphan check.
Minimum project size to run orphan detection.

metric_notes.definition: Flags isolated modules with no meaningful incoming or outgoing dependencies, indicating code that is unused or disconnected from the architecture.

calculation.raw_calculation: Require at least MIN_PROJECT_SIZE modules before scanning and for each module in module_dependency_graph.graph_nodes count how many graph_edges touch it. Any module whose incoming plus outgoing edge count is zero becomes an Orphan Module finding unless its base name equals or contains one of the ORPHAN_EXCLUDED_MODULES tokens; the reported file path is pulled from module_file_paths and the severity stays medium.
calculation.inputs: architectural.data.module_dependency_graph.graph_nodes, architectural.data.module_dependency_graph.graph_edges, architectural.data.module_file_paths plus the configuration values MIN_PROJECT_SIZE and ORPHAN_EXCLUDED_MODULES.
calculation.limitations: The dependency graph is built only from the statically recorded import relations, so dynamically constructed imports (importlib, __import__, runtime string evaluation) never contribute edges, and the module names arise from file-system paths with dots and no .py suffix. Small projects with fewer than MIN_PROJECT_SIZE modules are skipped entirely, and the simple substring-based ORPHAN_EXCLUDED_MODULES check can suppress valid modules whose path contains one of the forbidden tokens; when module_file_paths lacks an entry for a node the finding carries "Unknown" as its file location.

result_guide.Name: Orphan Module
result_guide.Description: Module '<module>' has no incoming or outgoing dependencies (project size >= MIN_PROJECT_SIZE).

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum cycle size.
Maximum cycle size.
Modules to exclude from cycle detection.
Cycle size for high severity.
Cycle strength for high severity.

metric_notes.definition: Flags dependency cycles between modules, which entangle components, hinder isolation, and make changes ripple unexpectedly.

calculation.raw_calculation: Enumerate every simple cycle reported by module_dependency_graph.graph_edges that fits between MIN_CYCLE_SIZE and MAX_CYCLE_SIZE and whose nodes do not contain any of the CYCLE_EXCLUDED_MODULES substrings. For each eligible cycle, compute a strength score by summing how many simple paths connect each node to its successor, group identical node sets together, and then choose the strongest occurrence. Assign severity "high" when both the cycle length and the strength meet or exceed CYCLE_HIGH_MIN_SIZE and CYCLE_HIGH_MIN_STRENGTH; otherwise keep "medium", and use module_file_paths to attach the earliest module in the cycle.
calculation.inputs: architectural.data.module_dependency_graph.graph_nodes, architectural.data.module_dependency_graph.graph_edges, architectural.data.module_file_paths plus thresholds MIN_CYCLE_SIZE, MAX_CYCLE_SIZE, CYCLE_EXCLUDED_MODULES, CYCLE_HIGH_MIN_SIZE, and CYCLE_HIGH_MIN_STRENGTH.
calculation.limitations: The graph only records statically parsed import relations, so runtime/deferred imports or reflection never contribute edges, and the node names derive from filesystem paths with dots rather than explicit module declarations; cycle strength is estimated by counting simple paths between adjacent cycle nodes, which can undercount mutual dependency intensity for very dense subgraphs, and missing entries in module_file_paths force the finding to fall back to "Unknown" for the file path.

result_guide.Name: Cyclic Dependency
result_guide.Description: Cycle size <cycle_size> within bounds MIN/MAX; strength <cycle_strength>.

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum total dependencies to consider instability.
Instability ratio threshold.

metric_notes.definition: Flags modules that depend heavily on more volatile modules than themselves, creating instability when upstream modules change.

calculation.raw_calculation: For every module in module_dependency_graph.graph_nodes build its incoming/outgoing counts from module_dependency_graph.graph_edges, skip modules whose dotted path contains 'test_', 'setup_', or '__init__', and for each module with at least MIN_DEPENDENCIES total connections compute instability as its outgoing count over the total. If that ratio exceeds UNSTABLE_DEPENDENCY_THRESHOLD emit an Unstable Dependency finding for the module using module_file_paths for location and leave severity at medium.
calculation.inputs: architectural.data.module_dependency_graph.graph_nodes, architectural.data.module_dependency_graph.graph_edges, architectural.data.module_file_paths plus thresholds MIN_DEPENDENCIES and UNSTABLE_DEPENDENCY_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: Dependency counts only reflect statically parsed import relations, so runtime import logic never produces edges, and filtered patterns are simple substring checks on the dotted module path; modules without an entry in module_file_paths report the file path as 'Unknown'.

result_guide.Name: Unstable Dependency
result_guide.Description: Stable module depends on less stable module; instability gap <gap> (> UNSTABLE_DEPENDENCY_THRESHOLD, deps >= MIN_DEPENDENCIES).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for number of methods.

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes that declare more methods than typical (NOM), signaling bloated interfaces or responsibilities.

calculation.pseudo-code:
nom_threshold = NOM_THRESHOLD
for class_name, class_data in structural.data.class_info.items():
    method_names = class_data.get('class_methods', [])
    regular_methods = [name for name in method_names
                       if not (name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'))]
    method_count = len(regular_methods)
    if method_count <= nom_threshold:
        continue
    severity = 'High' if method_count > nom_threshold * 1.5 else 'Medium'
    module_name = class_name.rsplit('.', 1)[0]
    file_path = structural.data.module_file_paths.get(module_name, 'Unknown')
    emit result for class_name with severity and counts
calculation.raw_calculation: Count every class in structural.data.class_info by measuring how many of its stored class_methods are not dunder-named; when that count exceeds NOM_THRESHOLD emit a finding and mark its severity as High if the count also exceeds 1.5x the threshold or Medium otherwise, reporting the module file path via structural.data.module_file_paths.
calculation.inputs: structural.data.class_info.class_methods for method counts, structural.data.module_file_paths for file locations, plus threshold NOM_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: class_methods lists only the method names and omits decorator metadata, so property-decorated methods cannot be filtered, and there is no way to distinguish methods that were implicitly added or inherited; missing module_file_paths entries result in 'Unknown' file locations.

result_guide.Name: High Number of Methods (NOM)
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' has <method_count> methods (> NOM_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for WMPC1 (complexity-based).
Threshold for WMPC2 (parameter-based).

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes whose combined method weight—complexity and parameter load—is unusually high (WMPC), indicating heavy behavior concentrated in one type.

calculation.pseudo-code:
threshold1 = WMPC1_THRESHOLD
threshold2 = WMPC2_THRESHOLD
for class_name, class_data in structural.data.class_info.items():
    method_names = class_data.get('class_methods', [])
    wmpc1 = 0
    wmpc2 = 0
    for method_name in method_names:
        complexity = complexity_from_method_ast(method_name)  # requires AST nodes that structural output does not expose
        parameter_count = params_from_method_ast(method_name)
        if complexity is None or parameter_count is None:
            continue
        wmpc1 += complexity
        wmpc2 += max(parameter_count - 1, 0)
    if wmpc1 > threshold1 or wmpc2 > threshold2:
        severity = 'High' if (wmpc1 > threshold1 * 1.5 or wmpc2 > threshold2 * 1.5) else 'Medium'
        module_name = class_name.rsplit('.', 1)[0]
        file_path = structural.data.module_file_paths.get(module_name, 'Unknown')
        emit finding for class_name with severity, wmpc1, wmpc2, file_path
calculation.raw_calculation: For each entry in structural.data.class_info compute the WMPC1 sum of cyclomatic complexity and the WMPC2 sum of destructed parameter counts from the class_methods that survive the special-method filter. When either summed value exceeds WMPC1_THRESHOLD or WMPC2_THRESHOLD emit the smell and mark it High whenever it also exceeds 1.5 times the same threshold, otherwise Medium, using module_file_paths for the located module.
calculation.inputs: structural.data.class_info.class_methods plus module_file_paths, with thresholds WMPC1_THRESHOLD and WMPC2_THRESHOLD (actual complexity/parameter counts require the method AST node that the extractor does not currently supply).
calculation.limitations: The structural AST payload only records method names rather than the AST nodes that the detector uses to compute cyclomatic complexity and parameter counts, so the per-method complexity score (for WMPC1) and the parameter count (WMPC2) must be reconstructed from the full AST if available; missing module_file_paths entries surface as 'Unknown'.

result_guide.Name: High Weighted Methods per Class (WMPC)
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' WMPC1 <wmpc1> or WMPC2 <wmpc2> exceeds WMPC thresholds.

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for SIZE2 (methods + fields).

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes that are oversized by SIZE2 (methods + fields), suggesting too much state or behavior packed into a single class.

calculation.pseudo-code:
threshold = SIZE2_THRESHOLD
for class_name, class_data in structural.data.class_info.items():
    method_names = class_data.get('class_methods', [])
    field_names = class_data.get('fields', [])
    method_calls = class_data.get('class_method_call_relations', {})
    significant_methods = [name for name in method_names
                           if not name.startswith('_')
                           or any(name in calls for calls in method_calls.values())]
    significant_fields = [name for name in field_names
                          if not name.startswith('_')
                          or any(name in calls for calls in method_calls.values())]
    size2 = len(significant_methods) + len(significant_fields)
    if size2 <= threshold:
        continue
    severity = 'High' if size2 > threshold * 1.5 else 'Medium'
    module_name = class_name.rsplit('.', 1)[0]
    file_path = structural.data.module_file_paths.get(module_name, 'Unknown')
    emit finding for class_name with size2, severity, and file_path
calculation.raw_calculation: Sum the non-private class_methods and fields from structural.data.class_info that are either public (not starting with '_') or referenced by another method call; when that SIZE2 value exceeds SIZE2_THRESHOLD emit the smell, bumping severity to High if the sum also exceeds 1.5 times the threshold, and look up the module file path for the report.
calculation.inputs: structural.data.class_info.class_methods, structural.data.class_info.fields, structural.data.class_info.class_method_call_relations, and structural.data.module_file_paths plus threshold SIZE2_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: The extractor only serializes method names and field names, so determining whether a field is actually referenced or a method is called elsewhere relies on the stored class_method_call_relations (which only tracks attribute names) and cannot reproduce the AST walk that could detect attribute usage; missing module_file_paths entries show as 'Unknown'.

result_guide.Name: Large Class (SIZE2)
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' SIZE2 value <size2> (> SIZE2_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for significant attributes.

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes with an unusually high number of significant fields (WAC), indicating large state surface and potential over-responsibility.

calculation.raw_calculation: Iterate through structural.data.class_info, skip uppercase constants, treat a field as significant if it is public or appears in multiple method call relations, count those fields as the WAC value, and whenever that sum exceeds WAC_THRESHOLD emit the smell with High severity only when the count also exceeds 1.5 times the threshold; look up module_file_paths to attach a location.
calculation.inputs: structural.data.class_info.fields, structural.data.class_info.class_method_call_relations, structural.data.module_file_paths, plus threshold WAC_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: The extractor only stores field names and the set of attribute names mentioned per method via class_method_call_relations, so the actual AST walk that checks for self.<field> occurrences (including private fields counted by usage frequency) cannot be replayed; uppercase detection relies purely on naming conventions, repeated usage is inferred by counting methods that mention the field rather than precise counts, and missing module_file_paths entries result in "Unknown".

result_guide.Name: High Weight of a Class (WAC)
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' WAC <wac> (> WAC_THRESHOLD).

elements.metric_name: High Lack of Cohesion of Methods (LCOM)

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for LCOM.

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes whose methods seldom share common state (high LCOM), indicating weak cohesion and fragmented responsibilities.

calculation.raw_calculation: From structural.data.class_info entries, filter out magic methods and keep those with at least two methods, then build a field usage map by checking which named fields also appear in class_method_call_relations for each method and by propagating those field sets along method-to-method call chains. Count every unordered pair of remaining methods, skip pairs of both private helpers, increment cohesive when they share a field and non-cohesive when they do not, compute LCOM as max(0, non_cohesive_pairs - cohesive_pairs), and report when that value exceeds LCOM_THRESHOLD (High when it also exceeds 1.5× the threshold) using module_file_paths to attach a location.
calculation.inputs: structural.data.class_info.class_methods, structural.data.class_info.fields, structural.data.class_info.class_method_call_relations, structural.data.module_file_paths plus threshold LCOM_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: The extractor only serializes method names, field names, and the attribute names that each method calls; there are no AST nodes or decorator data, so the original detection's AST.walk-based discovery of self.<field> references, direct field assignments, and property decorators cannot be reproduced, meaning the field usage map here is inferred from the limited call relations and may undercount shared state while still using module_file_paths when available (defaulting to 'Unknown' otherwise).

result_guide.Name: High Lack of Cohesion of Methods (LCOM)
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' LCOM <lcom> (> LCOM_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for RFC.

metric_notes.definition:
Detect classes with high Response for a Class (RFC).
Enhanced to consider:
- Method visibility and importance
- External vs internal calls
- Framework-specific methods
- Standard library calls

calculation.raw_calculation: For each class entry the detector counts every method that survives the special-method filter and every non-stdlib method call that does not resolve to another method on the same class, sums them to produce RFC, and emits a high-severity finding only when RFC exceeds 1.5× RFC_THRESHOLD; the report attaches module_file_paths for the class or falls back to "Unknown".
calculation.inputs: structural.data.class_info.class_methods, structural.data.class_info.class_method_call_relations, structural.data.module_file_paths plus threshold RFC_THRESHOLD and the standard library prefixes used for filtering.
calculation.limitations: The extractor only records method names and the attribute names referenced per method, so the AST.walk-based logic (control-flow detection to exclude simple helpers and direct `self.<field>`/`Call` node analysis that distinguishes internal vs external calls) cannot be replayed; external call detection here depends on simple name prefix checks and the available call lists, so public exposed methods might be misclassified and standard-library filtering is limited to the documented prefixes.

result_guide.Name: High Response for a Class (RFC)
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' RFC <rfc> (> RFC_THRESHOLD).

elements.metric_name: High Number of Classes per Module (NOCC)

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for number of classes per module.
Lower bound for avg weight adjustment.
Upper bound for avg weight adjustment.
Multiplier when avg weight is low.
Multiplier when avg weight is high.

metric_notes.definition: Flags modules that declare too many classes (NOCC), pointing to overcrowded files and weak modular breakdown.

calculation.raw_calculation: Group every class in structural.data.class_info by module after skipping test/Exception classes, derive an average weight per class as the mean of method count, field count, and cyclomatic complexity sum, adjust NOCC_THRESHOLD by multipliers if the average weight falls outside the configured bounds, and flag any module whose class count exceeds the adjusted threshold (High only when it also exceeds 1.5× the adjusted value).
calculation.inputs: structural.data.class_info.class_methods, .fields, .base_classes, structural.data.module_file_paths, plus thresholds NOCC_THRESHOLD, NOCC_AVG_WEIGHT_BOUND_LOW, NOCC_AVG_WEIGHT_BOUND_HIGH, NOCC_MULTIPLIER_LOW, NOCC_MULTIPLIER_HIGH.
calculation.limitations: Class weights depend on per-method cyclomatic complexity, but structural facts only list method names (no AST nodes or decorator/body data), so the actual complexity sum cannot be reconstructed from the extractor payload; module_file_paths may also be missing, causing the report to fall back to 'Unknown'.

result_guide.Name: High Number of Classes per Module (NOCC)
result_guide.Description: Module '<module>' has <class_count> classes (> adjusted NOCC_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for inheritance depth.
Bases to exclude from depth.

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes buried deep in inheritance hierarchies (DIT), which increases complexity and change risk.

calculation.raw_calculation: Build a directed graph from structural.data.class_info.base_classes while ignoring framework base names, mixin/interface/ABC patterns, compute the depth from 'object' for each class using BFS, and whenever the depth exceeds DIT_THRESHOLD emit a Medium finding (High if depth exceeds 1.5× the threshold) referencing module_file_paths.
calculation.inputs: structural.data.class_info.base_classes and structural.data.module_file_paths plus FRAMEWORK_BASES and DIT_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: Base-class references come only as strings in the facts payload, so skipping mixin/interface/abstract bases depends solely on naming heuristics, and the graph search cannot access AST nodes that explain why a class lacks a path from 'object'; missing module_file_paths entries yield 'Unknown'.

result_guide.Name: Deep Inheritance Tree (DIT)
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' inheritance depth <depth> (> DIT_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for effective LOC.
Multiplier for test files.
Doc complexity ratio breakpoint.
Multiplier when doc complexity is low.

metric_notes.definition: Flags files whose effective lines of code (LOC) exceed typical limits, indicating oversized or hard-to-maintain modules.

calculation.pseudo-code: threshold = LOC_THRESHOLD; for each module_info entry, re-open the file using module_file_paths, try common encodings until one works, split lines, track code/doc/import/blank counts while toggling a docstring flag when a stripped line starts with triple quotes, skip blank/comment/import lines, count the rest as code_lines, compute effective_loc from code_lines, adjust threshold upward for modules whose name contains "test" and for cases where code_lines/(total lines minus blank lines) is below LOC_DOC_COMPLEXITY_RATIO_BREAKPOINT, then emit a Medium finding whenever effective_loc exceeds the adjusted threshold and bump to High if it exceeds 1.5× that value, attaching the file path for the module.
calculation.raw_calculation: For every module_info record re-read the source file using module_file_paths, count non-blank lines that are not comments, imports, or part of triple-quoted docstrings to derive effective LOC, adjust LOC_THRESHOLD for test modules and low code/doc ratios, and flag files whose effective LOC exceeds the adjusted threshold (High if it exceeds 1.5×).
calculation.inputs: structural.data.module_info, structural.data.module_file_paths, and thresholds LOC_THRESHOLD, LOC_TEST_FILE_MULTIPLIER, LOC_DOC_COMPLEXITY_RATIO_BREAKPOINT, LOC_DOC_COMPLEXITY_MULTIPLIER.
calculation.limitations: The facts payload only provides module_file_paths and summary metadata, so this calculation must reopen each file with a fixed encoding list, docstrings are approximated by toggling on lines starting with triple quotes, and missing/unreadable files cause the module to be skipped; multi-line string delimiters inside expressions may still skew the counts.

result_guide.Name: High Lines of Code (LOC)
result_guide.Description: File '<file>' has <loc> LOC (> effective LOC_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for MPC.
Weight for external calls.

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes that send an unusually high number of method calls to other classes (MPC), indicating heavy outbound coupling.

calculation.raw_calculation: For each class the detector sums every outbound call not filtered by standard-library prefixes or framework helper-name patterns, weights the external count by MPC_EXTERNAL_WEIGHT, adds the distinct internal dependencies, and signals a smell whenever that weighted MPC exceeds MPC_THRESHOLD (raising severity to High when it exceeds 1.5× the threshold).
calculation.inputs: structural.data.class_info.class_methods, structural.data.class_info.class_method_call_relations, structural.data.module_file_paths, plus thresholds MPC_THRESHOLD and MPC_EXTERNAL_WEIGHT and the standard/file-filtering patterns.
calculation.limitations: The facts payload only lists method names and attribute-based call targets, so the AST walk that distinguishes call sites by object expressions cannot be replayed; this calculation depends on name-prefix heuristics to drop standard-library and framework helper calls, and modules with missing file paths report 'Unknown'.

result_guide.Name: High Message Passing Coupling (MPC)
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' MPC <mpc> (> MPC_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for CBO.
Weight for direct dependencies.
Weight for indirect dependencies.

metric_notes.definition: Flags classes coupled to many other classes (CBO), increasing ripple effects and reducing modularity.

calculation.raw_calculation: Filter each class's recorded method-call targets and base classes to remove standard-library, helper, and framework dependencies, count the remaining direct and indirect dependencies, weight them by CBO_DIRECT_WEIGHT/CBO_INDIRECT_WEIGHT, and report whenever that weighted sum exceeds CBO_THRESHOLD (Medium when it also exceeds 1.5×, High when it exceeds 2× the threshold).
calculation.inputs: structural.data.class_info.class_methods, structural.data.class_info.class_method_call_relations, structural.data.class_info.base_classes, structural.data.module_file_paths, plus thresholds CBO_THRESHOLD, CBO_DIRECT_WEIGHT, and CBO_INDIRECT_WEIGHT along with the detector's standard/framework filters.
calculation.limitations: The detector walks AST Call/Attribute nodes to find dependencies, but the extractor only emits name lists, so this approximation relies on the recorded call targets and helper-name heuristics; missing module_file_paths entries lead to 'Unknown' file locations.

result_guide.Name: High Coupling Between Object Classes (CBO)
result_guide.Description: Entity '<name>' CBO <cbo> (> CBO_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for number of children.
LOC breakpoint for high multiplier.
LOC breakpoint for medium multiplier.
Multiplier for high LOC.
Multiplier for medium LOC.

metric_notes.definition: Flags codebases where class hierarchies have too many children (NOC), indicating over-generalized parents or inheritance overuse.

calculation.raw_calculation: Assign each class to regular/test/utility/abstract buckets using name heuristics, compute weighted NOC = regular + 0.5×abstract + 0.3×utility, adjust NOC_THRESHOLD upward when production LOC exceeds the configured breakpoints, and report the project when weighted NOC exceeds that threshold (High when it exceeds 1.5×).
calculation.inputs: structural.data.class_info keys and summary lists plus structural.data.module_info[].lines_of_code and the LOC-based breakpoints/multipliers NOC_LOC_BREAKPOINT_HIGH/MEDIUM and NOC_LOC_MULTIPLIER_HIGH/MEDIUM in addition to NOC_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: The facts payload only exposes class names and module line counts, so bucket assignment depends on naming heuristics (test/helper/abstract keywords) rather than AST semantics and the precise cyclomatic/behavioral weight used in the detector cannot be reconstructed; modules lacking lines_of_code data or flagged as tests may skew the adjusted threshold.

result_guide.Name: High Number of Children (NOC)
result_guide.Description: Class '<name>' has <children> children (> adjusted NOC_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for cyclomatic complexity.

metric_notes.definition: Flags methods whose control-flow complexity (cyclomatic) is high, increasing testing and maintenance effort.

calculation.pseudo-code:
for class_name, info in structural.data.class_info.items():
+    for method in info.get('class_methods', []):
+        if method.startswith('__') and method.endswith('__'):
+            continue
+        complexity = calculate_cyclomatic_complexity(method_ast)  # detector walks the AST method node
+        threshold = CYCLOMATIC_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD
+        if complexity > threshold:
+            severity = 'High' if complexity > threshold * 1.5 else 'Medium'
+            module_name = class_name.rsplit('.', 1)[0]
+            file_path = structural.data.module_file_paths.get(module_name, 'Unknown')
+            emit finding for method with complexity, severity, and file_path
calculation.raw_calculation: For each method AST node reported under structural.data.class_info, count +1 for each If/Elif, loop, ExceptHandler, and boolean operation per `calculate_cyclomatic_complexity`, and whenever that sum exceeds CYCLOMATIC_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD emit a Medium finding (High when it also exceeds 1.5×) with the corresponding module file path.
calculation.inputs: structural.data.class_info.class_methods names plus the structural extraction of method AST nodes (needed to recompute control-flow statements) and structural.data.module_file_paths, together with CYCLOMATIC_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD.
calculation.limitations: The extractor currently drops AST method bodies and only returns method names, so the detailed control-flow counts (If/Elif/loops/Except/BoolOp nodes) the detector uses cannot be re-run until those AST nodes are exported; without them this description remains conceptual and the file path falls back to 'Unknown' when missing.

result_guide.Name: High Cyclomatic Complexity
result_guide.Description: Method '<name>' complexity <complexity> (> CYCLOMATIC_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for outgoing dependencies.

metric_notes.definition: Flags modules with too many outgoing dependencies (high fan-out), indicating broad reach and higher change blast radius.

calculation.raw_calculation: Recount each module_dependency_graph edge whose target is not a standard-library prefix, skip modules whose dotted name contains 'test', and when the number of such non-stdlib successors exceeds MAX_FANOUT report the module (High when it exceeds 1.5× the threshold) using module_file_paths for location.
calculation.inputs: structural.data.module_dependency_graph.graph_nodes, structural.data.module_dependency_graph.graph_edges, structural.data.module_file_paths, plus threshold MAX_FANOUT.
calculation.limitations: The dependency graph only encodes static import edges from the AST, so dynamic imports/external generation of dependencies are missing, and the standard_library list is hard-coded, so modules that rely on other stdlib names not listed still count toward fan-out. Missing module_file_paths entries fall back to 'Unknown'.

result_guide.Name: High Fan-out
result_guide.Description: Entity '<name>' fan-out <fan_out> (> MAX_FANOUT).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for incoming dependencies.

metric_notes.definition: Flags modules with too many incoming dependencies (high fan-in), making them hotspots whose changes impact many callers.

calculation.raw_calculation: Traverse structural.data.module_dependency_graph.graph_edges to count how many incoming edges each module has, skip modules matching utility/framework name patterns, and whenever that fan-in count exceeds MAX_FANIN report the module (High if it exceeds 1.5× the threshold) using module_file_paths for the file reference.
calculation.inputs: structural.data.module_dependency_graph.graph_nodes, structural.data.module_dependency_graph.graph_edges, structural.data.module_file_paths, plus threshold MAX_FANIN and the utility/framework name patterns used to skip noisy nodes.
calculation.limitations: The dependency graph is built from static import edges, so implicit/dynamic callers are absent, and the heuristics that drop utility/base/common modules depend solely on substring matches rather than precise classification; missing module_file_paths entries emit 'Unknown'.

result_guide.Name: High Fan-in
result_guide.Description: Entity '<name>' fan-in <fan_in> (> MAX_FANIN).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for meaningful lines in a file.

metric_notes.definition: Flags files whose length exceeds acceptable limits, signaling that code should be split into smaller, focused modules.

calculation.raw_calculation: Re-open each module file from structural.data.module_file_paths using a sequence of encodings, count non-empty, non-comment lines outside triple-quoted docstrings to produce a meaningful line count, and whenever that count exceeds MAX_FILE_LENGTH report the file (High when it exceeds 1.5× threshold).
calculation.inputs: structural.data.module_info and structural.data.module_file_paths plus threshold MAX_FILE_LENGTH.
calculation.limitations: Counting meaningful lines requires rereading each source file because the facts payload only carries summaries; docstrings are approximated using stripped line markers and multi-line strings that begin with triple quotes, so the count can drift if docstrings start/end mid-line or if encodings not tried are needed.

result_guide.Name: Long File
result_guide.Description: File '<file>' has <loc> meaningful LOC (> MAX_FILE_LENGTH).

metric_parameters.explanation: Threshold for branches.
Threshold for nesting depth.
Method prefixes to exclude from branch check.
Decorators to exclude from branch check.

metric_notes.definition: Flags methods with excessive branching and nesting, which hurt readability and increase error risk.

calculation.raw_calculation: For every method stored in structural.data.class_info, skip those whose names or decorators match the configured exclusion lists, traverse the stored AST-derived branch nodes to count If/loop/try occurrences plus elif/except extensions, track nesting as AK-based depth, and when the branch count exceeds MAX_BRANCHES or nesting depth exceeds MAX_NESTING_DEPTH emit a Medium finding (High if branch_count > 1.5× threshold) with the module file path.
calculation.inputs: structural.data.class_info.class_methods, structural.data.method_ast_nodes (branch metadata such as node types, elif counts, handler counts), structural.data.module_file_paths, configuration lists BRANCH_EXCLUDE_METHOD_PREFIXES/BRANCH_EXCLUDE_DECORATORS, and thresholds MAX_BRANCHES and MAX_NESTING_DEPTH.
calculation.limitations: The extractor currently only serializes method names not full AST nodes, so the branch count and nesting depth must be reconstructed from the stored node summaries; without those nodes the detector cannot reproduce the precise control-flow walk and the simplistic representation above is an approximation, while missing module_file_paths entries fall back to 'Unknown'.

result_guide.Name: Too Many Branches
result_guide.Description: Method '<name>' has <branch_count> branches and nesting <max_nesting> exceeding thresholds.
